scholarships.title: New Zealand Space Scholarship
scholarships.official_source: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), New Zealand Space Agency

existing.description: The New Zealand Space Scholarship gives postgraduate STEM students a fully supported three-month internship at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California, working alongside scientists and engineers on space missions and research. Applications for the 2027 scholarship opened on 1 October 2026 and the internship runs from July to September 2027. The scholarship covers return economy flights to the United States, accommodation, a daily living allowance and reasonable travel-related expenses including insurance support where applicable. Applicants must be New Zealand citizens aged 18 or over, enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities, and hold at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale.
eligibility: Be a New Zealand citizen (NASA requirement)
Be enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities
Hold a minimum GPA equivalent of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale, with New Zealand grades converted to the US GPA scale
Be proficient in written and spoken English (NASA requirement)
Be available to undertake the internship in person from July to September 2027 (dates subject to change)
Be willing to undergo any required health and security checks for travel to the United States and entry into US federal facilities
Be eligible for a J1 or F1 visa and understand the applicable visa conditions
Be able to obtain appropriate travel and medical insurance
Not currently hold, and never have held, citizenship in a country listed on NASA's Designated Countries List
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be New Zealand citizens (a NASA requirement), aged 18 or over, enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution in a field relevant to NASA's mission priorities, hold a minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale with New Zealand grades converted to the US scale, and be proficient in written and spoken English. They must be available in person from July to September 2027, willing to undergo any required health and security checks for US travel and entry to US federal facilities, eligible for a J1 or F1 visa, and able to obtain appropriate travel and medical insurance. Applicants who hold or have held citizenship of a country on NASA's Designated Countries List are not eligible.
benefits: Return economy flights to the United States
Accommodation in Southern California for the internship
Reasonable travel-related expenses including insurance support where applicable
Hands-on experience on NASA/JPL space missions and science projects
Networks and skills supporting careers in New Zealand's space and advanced aviation sectors
coverage: Return economy flights to the United States
Reasonable travel-related expenses, including insurance support where applicable
application_method: Apply online via the official application link published on the Ministry's scholarship page
Nominate up to two research areas that best match your studies
existing.selection_notes: The scholarship is highly competitive. Candidates are assessed on academic excellence, relevance of experience to JPL projects, personal qualities and self-management, and commitment to contributing to JPL and New Zealand's space sector. Final shortlisted candidates are submitted to JPL for final selection, so MBIE's assessment is not the final word.
existing.best_fit: New Zealand citizens aged 18 or over, enrolled in a postgraduate STEM qualification at a New Zealand tertiary institution, with at least a 3.0 GPA, whose field matches NASA's mission priorities and who can commit to three months in Southern California from July to September 2027.
existing.notes: This is an internship placement, not a degree award, so no tuition fees arise and the value is not published as a single figure; the Ministry publishes only the categories covered. NASA imposes several of the eligibility rules, notably New Zealand citizenship, English proficiency and the Designated Countries List exclusion, and JPL makes the final selection decision. Students completing their current qualification before 2027 may still apply if they intend to enrol in postgraduate study at a New Zealand tertiary institution and can provide proof of enrolment before the scholarship is awarded.
existing.duration: 3-month internship, July to September 2027 (dates subject to change)
existing.application_period: The 2027 round opened on 1 October 2026 and is open now. The internship itself runs July to September 2027. No closing date is published on the official page.
existing.deadline_display: The Ministry states "Applications for the 2027 New Zealand Space Scholarship open on 1 October 2026" but publishes no closing date for the 2027 round on this page.
existing.program_type: Government-funded postgraduate research internship placement abroad (not a degree programme)
